entries.name: GitHub
entries.description: Search and read your repositories, issues and pull requests.

setup.title: Create a personal access token
setup.text: Open GitHub's token settings and create a fine-grained personal access token. Give it read access to the repositories you want Haruspex to see — it does not need write access for the tools enabled by default.

setup.label: Personal access token
setup.help: Starts with github_pat_ or ghp_. Stored with your other Haruspex settings.

entries.name: Google Drive & Sheets
entries.description: Search and read your Google Drive files, and read or update Google Sheets.

setup.title: Create a Google Cloud project
setup.text: Open the Google Cloud console and create a new project (or pick an existing one). This is free, and it is what lets your own account authorise Haruspex.

setup.title: Enable the Drive and Sheets APIs
setup.text: In the same project, enable the Google Drive API and the Google Sheets API. Without these the sign-in will succeed and every request will fail.

setup.title: Create an OAuth client
setup.text: Under APIs & Services → Credentials, create an OAuth client ID with application type 'Desktop app'. Configure the consent screen first if you are asked to. Then download the client's JSON file — you will need it in the next step.

setup.label: OAuth client JSON file
setup.help: The file you just downloaded. Haruspex copies it into this server's own folder and renames it; the original is left where it is.

setup.label: OAuth client ID
setup.help: Shown on the credentials page, and also inside the JSON file you just chose.

setup.label: OAuth client secret
setup.help: Shown next to the client ID.

setup.label: Sign in to Google
setup.help: Opens your browser once so you can grant access. Sign in with an account that belongs to the Cloud project's organisation.

entries.name: Blender
entries.description: Inspect and edit the scene in a running copy of Blender.

companion.hint: In Blender, press N in the 3D viewport, open the MCP tab, and click Start MCP Server.

setup.title: Install Blender 3.0 or newer
setup.text: Haruspex talks to a copy of Blender running on this machine; it does not install or bundle one. If you already have Blender, skip this step.

setup.label: Install the Blender add-on
setup.help: Copies the add-on into Blender's add-ons folder. Blender should be closed while this runs.

setup.title: Turn the add-on on
setup.text: Open Blender, then Edit → Preferences → Add-ons and enable 'Interface: MCP for Blender'. Back in the 3D viewport, press N, open the MCP tab, and click Start MCP Server. Haruspex can only see Blender while that server is running.

setup.label: Sketchfab API key (optional)
setup.help: Only needed if you want the assistant to download models from Sketchfab. Leave blank otherwise.

setup.label: Poly Pizza API key (optional)
setup.help: Only needed for Poly Pizza's low-poly asset library. Leave blank otherwise.

entries.name: Godot
entries.description: Build and inspect scenes in a running Godot editor.

companion.hint: Open the Godot project you want to work on, and make sure the Godot MCP plugin is enabled for it under Project → Project Settings → Plugins. The plugin is per project, so a different project needs it enabled too.

setup.title: Install Godot 4.4 or newer
setup.text: Haruspex talks to a Godot editor running on this machine; it does not install or bundle one.

setup.title: Add the plugin to your project
setup.text: In Godot, open the project you want to work on, then Editor → Asset Library and search for 'Godot MCP'. Install it into the project. This is per project, not per machine — another project needs it added too.

setup.title: Enable it
setup.text: Project → Project Settings → Plugins, and switch 'Godot MCP' on. It connects to Haruspex by itself; the order you start things in does not matter.
